title: Isosceles-free sets in the honeycomb grid
statement: Let the honeycomb grid H_N be the points (a, b) of the triangular grid T_N (the points a + b w, w = e^(i pi/3), a, b >= 0, a + b <= N - 1) with a - b not divisible by 3. Removing the index-3 sublattice of hexagon centres from the triangular lattice leaves the honeycomb lattice of graphene, with unit bonds; the squared distance is da^2 + da db + db^2. Determine the largest number of points of the honeycomb grid H_N such that no point is equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included: no point is the midpoint of two others), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 12; the headline cell is N = 14: find 16 or more such points of the region of side 14 (an upper bound is 53).
submission: Text file: one point 'a b' per line, a point of the region of side 14 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 15 points of the region of side 14 with no point equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is isosceles-free when no point of it is equidistant from two others: no three of its points form an isosceles triangle, counting the flat case of a point midway between two others. For the n x n square grid the largest such sets have become a test bed for machine-assisted constructions: PatternBoost (Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner and Williamson, 2024) and AlphaEvolve (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 2025) found sets of 108 to 112 points in the 64 x 64 grid, the first values are OEIS A271907, and the best lower bound proved, of order n sqrt(log log n / log n) (arXiv:2610.04194, 2026), is far from the subquadratic upper bounds (the grid question is Erdos problem #1207). The honeycomb lattice (the carbon sites of graphene) is the triangular lattice with a third of its points removed; it has no unit equilateral triangles, but its distances are still Loschian numbers. The exact values grow roughly like N; whether the growth stays linear, and how it compares with the triangular grid (whose isosceles-free sets contain those of the honeycomb grid), is open.
references: F. Charton, J. S. Ellenberg, A. Z. Wagner, G. Williamson, PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI, arXiv:2411.00566 (2024)
B. Georgiev, J. Gomez-Serrano, T. Tao, A. Z. Wagner, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale, arXiv:2511.02864 (2025)
Sparse coloring for isosceles-free grids: an AI-assisted proof case study, arXiv:2610.04194 (2026)
OEIS A271907 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: isosceles-free subsets are studied for the n x n square grid (OEIS A271907, PatternBoost, AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2610.04194); no result was found for the honeycomb grid, and its first values are not in the OEIS.
closest: The n x n square grid (OEIS A271907; PatternBoost arXiv:2411.00566; AlphaEvolve arXiv:2511.02864; arXiv:2610.04194): the same question in another lattice.
Erdos-type questions on isosceles sets in the plane and in space: point sets in which every three points form an isosceles triangle, the opposite extreme.

baseline.text: 15 for N = 14, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/hex-isosceles.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..12: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 10, 13, 14 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py). Upper bound for N = 14: 53 (every chosen point sees the others at different distances, and no point of the region sees more than 52 different distances).
